hub.author: Brian Foster
hub.text: Before Thursday's flow review I want the queue manager to be a real epic. Right now it is one ticket, and Vincent's flow pass is a sheet on its own. I left a note on the ticket about how I want it. One child for each area, and every report gets its line under the right child. Please also put a stock-take sheet in your ZM queue manager folder and share it with everyone on the review invite, Leonard too, and add one slide with the numbers to your queue manager deck. When it is done tell me here how many reports are passed, how many wait on QA, how many wait on a fix, how many areas are clear and how many reports are on the review list.

epic_note.author: Brian Foster
epic_note.text:
How I want this epic.

Children: Tutorials, Level-end rewards, Daily Gift, Season Pass, Collect & Win, Win Streak, Zombie Lane, Boss Arena, Endless Mode, Card packs. One child each, same team, no assignee.

Reports: the rows of Vincent's flow pass sheet, all of them. For Vincent that sheet is the list, so don't add new reports from his chats, and his Bug Checklist canvas and the Collect & Win canvas stay as they are. Plus any bug somebody else on the team saw in a build and told you about in a DM since Vincent started his pass on the 26th, about the home screen after a level. If it is already a row, don't count it twice. The skip tutorial exceptions Oliver has in #zombie-bugs and the input blocker I parked are not on the sheet and stay off.

Status of a report, as it stands today, one of three. Passed: Vincent's ok or nr on a build that counts under Arthur's rule for QA passes, as long as that pass still stands under his rule. Waiting on QA: not passed, and a fix for it is in main that QA has not tried on a main build yet. Waiting on a fix: everything else.

Line under the child: if a ticket already has the report, move that ticket under the child and leave a note with the status and why. If its state does not match the status, put Done for Passed, In Validation for Waiting on QA, Todo for Waiting on a fix. If no ticket has it, make a sub-issue under the child with the report as the title and the state the same way. No priority and no assignee on the new ones, that is Julia's point about your tickets, I will set them.

A child is Clear when all its reports are Passed, otherwise Open. Set the child to Done if it is Clear and to Todo if it is Open.

Review list: a report that is not Passed, in an area on the agenda of Thursday's review.

Sheet: tab Reports with Report, Area, Status, Ticket, Review list, Why. Tab Areas with Area, Status, Open reports. Slide: the five numbers I asked you for.

legend.author: Vincent Parker
legend.text:
How to read my pass sheets

Found on: the build I first saw it on.
Ticket: the Linear key if I filed one.
Fix: the PR the dev told me it went into. Blank if nobody told me.
Re-test: ok and a build means it is fine on that build. nr and a build means I could not make it happen on that build. again and a build means it still happens. ok, chat means I told the dev ok in our chat, the build is there. Blank means not re-tested yet.

rule_doc.author: Arthur Blake
rule_doc.text:
ZM builds and QA passes

Internal, Android and Submission are only the jobs. What matters is the branch. For ZM a QA pass only counts on a build of the main branch. A build of a feature branch is for the dev to check their own work, so a pass there has to be done again once the branch is merged.

If you want QA to look at a branch build before you merge, that is fine and it saves time, just don't call it passed.

A pass stands until somebody sees the bug again on a main build made after the one it passed on. Then it is open again, whoever saw it.

Which branch a build came from is in its #builds post.

dd_doc.author: Arthur Blake
dd_doc.text:
DD hotfix builds and QA passes

For DD hotfixes a pass on the dev's branch build is enough, we cherry-pick those straight onto the release branch.

Anything that is not a hotfix goes through develop and gets its pass there.
